title: The Path of Relationship
speaker: Nomon Tim Burnett
summary: Nomon Tim Burnett takes up Dogen's "Ango" chapter from the Shobogenzo, which treats the practice period as peaceful abiding, as the close of the winter practice period nears. Nomon recalls the Buddha's monsoon-season retreats and Sharon Salzberg's account of wading through flooded Kolkata streets, then reads Dogen's quotation of Ru Jing's poem about piling up bones in an open field. Dogen's line that the practice period "requires unstinting support" leads to a silent reflection on how each person has been supported over the last ninety days. Listeners then divide into groups of four or five for a round of speaking and deep listening, and the evening closes with chants and announcements about learning the bells.
